Class ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.occurrences.SysMLOccurrence

sysmlinjava.analysis.ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase
All Implemented Interfaces:
AttributeObserver, ObservableAttribute, StateBehaviorContext
public abstract class ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase extends ParametricAnalysisCase
SysMLinJava representation of the SysMLv1 objective function constraint block.

Specialized parametric analysis

A specialized type of parametric analysis, the ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase simply extends the ParametricAnalysisCase with parameters that represent measures of effectiveness, performance, and/or suitability, and with one or more constraints that declare the objective function to be satisfied by the parameters.

Parameters as MOP, MOE, MOS

As an abstract class, the ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase is specialized for a particular type of analysis that involves the calculation of a constraint defining an objective function using parameters for the moes, mops, and/or mos's. Parameters should be annotated in accordance with their purpose in this regard, i.e. as a
  • @MeasureOfEffectiveness,
  • @MeasureOfPerformance, or
  • @MeasureOfSuitability.
The mop, moe, and mos parameters for the ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase should be declared locally in the extended class. As with any extension of the ParametricAnalysisCase, the constraint (objective function) must first retrieve the current values of the bound values for the mop, moe, and mos parameters from the params map.

Objective Function Constraints

In the rare case where more than one constraint is needed to define the objective function, the additional constraints can be declared in the objective function analysis case. These specialized constraints should be annotated with @ObjectiveFunction to identify them as such. The objective function constraint should be defined in the createObjectiveFunctions() method.

Objective function analysis case creation same as for parametrice analysis

Other aspects of the specialized ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase are essentially the same as for any ParametricAnalysisCase, i.e. creating the parameters, creating attributes, etc. as well as the constraints for the objective function.

      Overridable method to perform the analysis case action. The perform() method can be overridden to perform a custom action for the analysis case as needed.     • createObjectiveFunction

      protected void createObjectiveFunction()
      Overridable operation that should create the objective function's constraint i.e. the objectiveFunction. The objectiveFunction should define the objective function that calculates the objective metric. An example follows: 
              @Parameter
        DistanceMeters accuracy;
        @Parameter
        Availability availability;
        @Parameter
        Cost$US cost;

        @Attribute
        RReal accuracyWeight;
        @Attribute
        RReal availabilityWeight;
        @Attribute
        RReal costWeight;

        @MeasureOfEffectiveness
        RReal moe;
                :
        @ConstraintFunction
        MyMOEFunction myMOEFunction;
                :

        @Override
        protected void createFunction()
        {
                myMOEFunction = () ->
                {
                        moe.setValue(accuracy.multipliedBy(accuracyWeight)
          .addedTo(availability.multipliedBy(availabilityWeight)
          .addedTo(cost.multipliedBy(costWeight)));
                };
        }
                :
        @Override
        protected void createObjectiveFunction()
        {
                objectiveFunction = new SysMLConstraint(myMOEFunction, "moe = sum of weighted accuracy, availability, and cost", "objectiveFunction", 0L);
        }
      See Also:
      • ObjectiveFunction

    • createMeasuresOfEffectiveness

      protected void createMeasuresOfEffectiveness()
      Overridable operation that should create the objective function analysis case's measure-of-effectivenss parameters by "put"-ing initialized instances of each into the params map with their appropriate "key"s, i.e. their parameter IDs. An example follows: 
      
	&#64;MeaureOfEffectiveness
 	FirstMeasureOfEffectiveness firstMOE;
	&#64;MeaureOfEffectiveness
 	NextMeasureOfEffectiveness nextMOE;
	&#64;MeaureOfEffectiveness
 	LastMeasureOfEffectiveness lastMOE;
 		:
	&#64;Override
	protected void createMeasures()
	{
		FirstMOE = new FirstMeasureOfEffectiveness(<i>initializer</i>);
		NextMOE = new NextMeasureOfEffectiveness(<i>initializer</i>);
		LastMOE = new LastMeasureOfEffectiveness(<i>initializer</i>);

		params.put("FirstMeasureOfEffectiveness", FirstMOE));
		params.put("NextMeasureOfEffectiveness", NextMOE);
		params.put("LastMeasureOfEffectiveness", LastMOE);
	}
      If no measures-of-effectiveness are calculated by the objective function, then the method should be empty.
      See Also:
      • SysMLAttributeType
      • MeasureOfEffectiveness

    • createMeasuresOfSuitability

      protected void createMeasuresOfSuitability()
      Overridable abstract operation that should create the objective function analysis case's measure-of-suitability parameters by "put"-ing initialized instances of each into the params map with their appropriate "key"s, i.e. their parameter IDs. An example follows: 
      
	&#64;MeaureOfSuitability
 	FirstMeasureOfSuitability firstMOS;
	&#64;MeaureOfSuitability
 	NextMeasureOfSuitability nextMOS;
	&#64;MeaureOfSuitability
 	LastMeasureOfSuitability lastMOS;
 		:
	&#64;Override
	protected void createMeasures()
	{
		FirstMOS = new FirstMeasureOfSuitability(<i>initializer</i>);
		NextMOS = new NextMeasureOfSuitability(<i>initializer</i>);
		LastMOS = new LastMeasureOfSuitability(<i>initializer</i>);

		params.put("FirstMeasureOfSuitability", FirstMOS));
		params.put("NextMeasureOfSuitability", NextMOS);
		params.put("LastMeasureOfSuitability", LastMOS);
	}
      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the MeasureOfSuitability annotation and XxxxMeasureOfSuitability() is a constructor of any SysMLValueType class. The measure constraint parameter must be a SysMLValueType type or an extension of the SysMLValueType.

      If no measures-of-suitability are calculated by the objective function, then the method should be empty.
